channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Caiado defende ampliar prerrogativa dos governadores na segurança pública: 'legislar em alguns crimes'
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), a presidential candidate, stated he intends to expand governors' prerogatives in public security, allowing states to legislate on specific crimes within their territories. He pledged to create a Ministry of Public Security and provide support in intelligence, Coaf, and the Federal Revenue to fight organized crime, criticizing the Lula administration for interfering in state autonomy. He also advocated for a regulatory framework on artificial intelligence and legislation on rare earths to diversify Brazilian exports.

item.title: Faculdades privadas dizem que Caiado revela desconhecimento sobre cursos de Medicina
item.description: Abmes stated that PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado demonstrates ignorance regarding medical education in Brazil. The association advocates for public policies ensuring quality and regulation in higher education, particularly in courses such as Medicine.

item.title: “Com o PT, o escândalo nunca é ponto fora da curva”, diz Marinho
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign coordinator, Senator Rogério Marinho, criticized the PT by claiming scandals are a 'method' of the party, not exceptions. He referenced recent investigations involving businessman Fábio Luís Lula da Silva but did not directly name Lula.

item.title: “Se o Fábio Luís não fosse filho do presidente Lula, esse inquérito teria sido arquivado”
item.description: Marco Aurélio Carvalho, lawyer defending Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, claimed that investigations against the president's son would not proceed if he did not share the same surname as the head of the Executive, implying political bias. The defense questions the motives behind the probes.

item.title: Nunes cobra nome de Flávio em santinhos de aliados: "Tem que ter o 22"
item.description: São Paulo mayor Ricardo Nunes demanded that candidates from Tarcísio’s coalition include Flávio Bolsonaro’s name and number on campaign leaflets, reinforcing the alliance. Nunes has led outreach efforts for Flávio in the capital, organizing agendas and meetings with businessmen and councilors. Governor Tarcísio showed less visibility in the support actions.

item.title: A nova pesquisa de intenção de voto para presidente, com 6 mil entrevistados
item.description: The legal website Jota will release on August 26, 2026, a presidential voting intention poll with 6,000 respondents. The survey will test runoff scenarios involving Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Fernando Haddad, while also assessing voter rejection and government approval.

item.title: Com desempate de Nunes Marques, TSE libera Crivella para disputar Senado
item.description: Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled 4-3, with a tie-breaking vote by Justice Nunes Marques, to allow Marcelo Crivella to run for a Senate seat in the October elections. Crivella is a former mayor of Rio de Janeiro, current federal deputy, and a member of the Republicans party.

item.title: Tarcísio apoia Flávio negando São Tomé: ver para não crer
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas outlined his national political ambitions during a pair of interviews, telling Grupo Globo outlets that Flávio Bolsonaro would honor a pledge to end presidential reelection if elected. A day earlier, the São Paulo governor told Jovem Pan he 'might' run for the presidency in the future, cementing his role in the presidential race.

item.title: Lulinha processa Flávio Bolsonaro e pede indenização por vídeo com IA sobre suspeitas desvios do INSS
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, sued Flávio Bolsonaro over an AI-generated campaign video linking him to the INSS social security fraud scandal, seeking R$10,000 in damages and removal of the content within 24 hours. His defense argues there is no formal investigation or charge against him regarding INSS fraud, only inquiries into alleged influence trafficking at the Supreme Court. Lulinha also filed a similar lawsuit against presidential candidate Romeu Zema, but a São Paulo court has already denied the removal request in that case.

item.title: Governo Lula envia 19 toneladas de arroz à Colômbia após terremoto
item.description: Lula's government sent 19 tons of rice to Colombia as humanitarian aid following a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that killed at least 314 people. The shipment, carried by the Brazilian Air Force, does not affect national food supplies.

item.title: Viana pede que ministérios enviem dados sobre negócios de Lulinha
item.description: Senator Carlos Viana filed information requests with three ministries to investigate Lulinha's involvement in government negotiations, including deals involving cannabidiol and Telebras. He also requested precautionary measures from the Supreme Court to preserve evidence and prevent loss of data regarding payments and public contacts.

item.title: Senador quer saber se grupo de Lulinha teve encontros com autoridades do governo
item.description: Senator Carlos Viana (PSD-MG) requested information from federal ministries regarding alleged meetings between government officials and lobbyists close to Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, including Roberta Luchsinger, as revealed by PF investigations. A VEJA report detailed a lobbying scheme linked to federal contracts, with suspicions of personal payments to President Lula's relatives. Viana also asked the STF to preserve data from the investigated group's communications.

item.title: Áudio: Sete organizações internacionais vão acompanhar as eleições de outubro
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) confirmed that seven international organizations will act as independent observers in the 2026 elections. The entities include the OAS, Mercosur Parliament, European Union, Arab League, and others, to ensure transparency and integrity of the electoral process.

item.title: A colaboração de Beltrame no plano de governo do candidato de Lula a governador de SC
item.description: José Mariano Beltrame, former head of Rio de Janeiro's Public Security, collaborated on the government plan of Gelson Merisio, Lula's candidate for governor of Santa Catarina. The information was revealed in an exclusive subscriber-only article.

item.title: Brasil envia ajuda humanitária à Colômbia após terremoto
item.description: Brazil sent humanitarian aid to Colombia after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake left over 300 dead and 260 missing. A Brazilian Air Force aircraft departed with 19 tons of rice bound for the city of Pereira.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula já deveria ser investigado?
item.description: Lawyer André Fini states that President Lula's knowledge of lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger's work with his son is not enough to investigate him. He emphasizes that proof of willful blindness to irregularities would be required to establish a corruption crime.

item.title: Lula anuncia edital para compra de supercomputador de R$ 1 bilhão
item.description: President Lula announced a bidding process for a R$1 billion supercomputer to be installed in Rio Grande do Norte, with operations expected by late 2027, as part of the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan. The government also announced a partnership with Chinese companies Huawei and iFlytek, with R$1.2 billion in investments over five years for Portuguese-language AI development. Additional measures include the creation of a National Center for Algorithmic Transparency at UFMG, with R$50 million, and technical cooperation agreements.

item.title: Vice de Flávio entra em disputa política com Motta sobre escolta para fazer campanha
item.description: Deputy Alfredo Gaspar, running as vice-president alongside Flávio Bolsonaro, had his request for a legislative police escort denied by Chamber President Hugo Motta, who cited that the candidacy does not qualify for protection. Gaspar sarcastically accepted the decision and stated he will campaign without an escort, relying on divine protection.

item.title: Equipe de deputado do PL e estudantes entram em confronto em campus da UFBA
item.description: Staff members of Bahia state deputy Diego Castro (PL) clashed with UFBA students after the lawmaker removed stickers of Lula and Jerônimo Rodrigues from the Ondina campus in Salvador. The incident occurred amid ongoing local and national electoral competition.

item.title: Mendonça deve manter no STF investigações sobre tráfico de influência de Lulinha
item.description: Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça is likely to reject the request from the Attorney General's Office to send investigations into alleged influence peddling by Fábio Luís Lula to the lower court. The decision keeps the case at the federal level, preventing referral to lower instances. The Public Ministry had requested the forwarding of the proceedings for grassroots judicial investigation.

item.title: Ao vivo: Flávio realiza live em seu canal do YouTube
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), presidential candidate, holds a live stream on Thursday (20) at 7 PM on YouTube, part of weekly broadcasts since July. The approach mirrors the direct communication style used by his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Caso Lulinha: guerra de bastidores escancara sistema de poder
item.description: Columnist Fernando Schüler analyzes investigations involving Lulinha and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, stating the case exposes a political 'behind-the-scenes war' driven by the proximity of the 2026 elections. Schüler claims there is an operation to delay or block the probe, while pressure mounts for transparency regarding how power is structured in Brazil.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Amiga de Lulinha diz em mensagem que conversou com Lula
item.description: The 'Papo Antagonista' program discusses a Federal Police investigation into an alleged influence peddling scheme involving Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, son of President Lula. A friend of Lulinha reportedly sent messages indicating contact with the president's son.

item.title: A grande lacuna da eleição
item.description: The climate crisis impacts Brazil's economy, health, and security but is addressed secondarily in the 2026 elections. The author questions the absence of a robust environmental agenda in government programs. Polluting industry companies lead sponsorships of climate events, highlighting a gap between economic interests and public policies.

item.title: Como Marçal pode ajudar Lula a vencer no 1º turno
item.description: Pablo Marçal's candidacy could help Lula win in the first round by siphoning votes from right-wing candidates and being disqualified later, thereby reducing the number of valid votes needed to win.

item.title: Haddad rejeita sugestão de impeachment a ministros do STF: "Cautela"
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) rejected during his São Paulo campaign the suggestion of impeaching STF justices proposed by Tarcísio de Freitas, advocating caution to avoid politicizing judicial actions. He stated that all citizens and public officials are subject to the law, but criticized actions driven by political convenience. Haddad also mocked Tarcísio by calling him 'concurseiro' during a previous debate.

item.title: Com PF, Abin e Forças Armadas, Nunes Marques monta estrutura de segurança para as eleições de 2026
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques established two new bodies to ensure security and normality for the 2026 elections. The Niae focuses on protecting infrastructure and people, while the Nigde works on preventing crimes and ensuring legal conduct.

item.title: Mendonça manda derrubar vídeo que associa Flávio a Vorcaro
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered the removal of an AI-generated video on Instagram linking Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Pan. The content was deemed potentially misleading and subject to disinformation. The decision aims to ensure the integrity of electoral information.

item.title: Tirar a poeira dos arquivos
item.description: The documentary 'Anistia 79' reveals previously unseen footage from the 1979 Rome Conference, highlighting the Brazilian diaspora's resistance against the amnesty granted to torture perpetrators of the dictatorship. Director Anita Leandro recovers testimonies from survivors and uses archives found at Nanterre University to contextualize the legacy of authoritarian-era traumas in contemporary Brazil. The film is part of a cinematic movement that reinterprets national history through archival material.

item.title: Terra retomada
item.description: Eduardo Paes (PSD) secured strategic alliances in the Baixada Fluminense, winning support from traditional bolsonarismo figures like Rogério Lisboa (PP) and Jane Reis (sister of former Duque de Caxias mayor Washington Reis). These alliances weaken support for Flávio Bolsonaro in the region, strengthening Paes' trajectory in an electoral college accounting for 22% of Rio de Janeiro's electorate.

item.title: Onde as direitas se encontram
item.description: Maria Inês Nassif, a journalist and social scientist, contributed to major Brazilian media outlets and served as an advisor at the Instituto Lula, associated with former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Her work emphasizes critical analysis of themes like corruption and democratic governance.

item.title: O crime é outro
item.description: A Federal Police investigation identifies Maranhão governor Carlos Brandão as the alleged leader of a criminal organization linked to a 2022 assassination in São Luís. The arrest of a blogger's source, connected to the same group, triggered backlash against the Supreme Court, including accusations of press censorship and threats of international sanctions. The case gains national prominence ahead of the 2026 elections, involving the Brandão family and Supreme Court justices Alexandre de Moraes and Flávio Dino.

item.title: Os desafios de Lula
item.description: Lula's campaign faces a challenging start, with a technical tie against Flávio Bolsonaro in the Quaest poll's second-round simulation dated August 14th. Despite a slight improvement in the government's approval in July, the president is on the defensive regarding public security and corruption, the top concerns among voters.

item.title: Marçal é “do bem e preparado”, diz Flávio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), presidential candidate, stated that Pablo Marçal (PRTB) is a 'well-intentioned and prepared' person during a public event with São Paulo mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB). The statement was made to journalists on Thursday, the 20th.

item.title: Zema propõe tarifa mínima para motoboys de aplicativos
item.description: Zema proposed a minimum fare for app-based delivery workers during a meeting in São Paulo, stating it would be a priority for implementation at the start of his term. He also advocated for improving the Individual Entrepreneur Register (MEI) to formalize delivery workers and reiterated support for a CLT alternative based on hourly work.

item.title: Nossas escolhas
item.description: CartaCapital launches 'Our Choices', indicating 2026 electoral preferences, reinforcing editorial tradition. Criticizes opponent as 'family interests goon', promoting national sovereignty. Electoral campaign began on October 16, influencing Congress and foreign policy.

item.title: Alhos e bugalhos
item.description: New leaks from the Federal Police involving President Lula's son, Fábio Luís da Silva, and allies like Roberta Luchsinger and Marco Aurélio Santana (Marcola) have sparked fresh political backlash, with allegations of corruption and influence peddling. Lula's defense team challenges the legality of the message disclosure and demands investigations into possible unauthorized leaks.

item.title: O Brasil real
item.description: The leadership of the Museum of the Inconfidence in Ouro Preto, headed by Alex Calheiros, is pushing for the decolonization of exhibitions, sparking protests from conservative sectors that accuse curators of distorting Brazilian history. The debate mirrors national tensions over how to retell colonial memory and its connection to slavery.

item.title: O Trump mineiro
item.description: Plínio Vicentin Júnior, a Novo candidate for federal deputy in Minas Gerais, adopts the persona of Donald Trump to attract votes, touring the Central Market of Belo Horizonte to produce social media content. His performance is marked by criticism of the federal government and defense of Minas products, but avoids comments about Governor Romeu Zema, his party colleague.

item.title: Cartas Capitais
item.description: The text presents Lula as a candidate for reelection with support for a left-wing Congress, emphasizing the importance of working-class organization. It also mentions Benedita da Silva as a candidate, referencing her political trajectory. The content has an electoral and progressive tone.

item.title: Olho por olho?
item.description: The Brazilian government considers adopting reciprocity in response to US tariffs, but pledges to consult business leaders before taking action. Experts view this stance as political, emphasizing the need to counter Trump's pressures, which may influence Brazilian elections. 52% of Brazilians believe the tariff hike aims to support Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Petróleo na Foz do Amazonas
item.description: Petrobras announced the discovery of oil in the Morpho well, located in the Equatorial Margin, approximately 175 kilometers off the coast of Amapá. The company's president, Magda Chambriard, emphasized the significant potential of the find, though no volume estimates are available yet. Following the discovery, Senator Davi Alcolumbre announced measures to support President Lula's agenda, including advances on key projects such as the Security Constitutional Amendment and pension reform.

item.title: Lugar de criança
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies revived PEC 32/15, which lowers the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16, during the electoral period. Legal experts warn that the measure may further criminalize teenagers and deepen racial inequality in the justice system. The move is seen as an electoral maneuver, with candidates like Flávio Bolsonaro including the proposal in their campaign platforms.

item.title: Ibovespa tem leve baixa e dólar sobe com novas tensões no Oriente Médio
item.description: The Ibovespa posted a slight gain driven by Petrobras and Vale, while the dollar rose to BRL 5.19 due to geopolitical tensions and election uncertainty. Banks showed mixed performance, with Itaú and Bradesco declining. Foreign capital flight and fiscal risk are challenging the Brazilian market.

item.title: Haddad diz que impeachment de ministro do STF exige cautela e não pode ser usado por 'conveniência política'
item.description: Haddad stated that STF ministers are subject to the law, but defended caution in using impeachment to avoid politicizing the judiciary, especially when driven by political convenience.

item.title: Casas Bahia vira munição de Tarcísio contra economia de Lula
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas used the bankruptcy protection filing of Casas Bahia as ammunition against Lula's economic policy during a campaign event in São Paulo alongside Flávio Bolsonaro and Ricardo Nunes. The governor criticized the situation faced by entrepreneurs, citing lack of credit, indebtedness, and legal uncertainty. Flávio Bolsonaro had already recorded campaign material in front of a closed Casas Bahia store in Brasília, linking the crisis to high interest rates.

item.title: Flávio confirma visita à maior feira do agro da América Latina
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed attendance at Expointer in Rio Grande do Sul on August 2, accompanying gubernatorial candidate Luciano Zucco. The visit comes amid attacks from Ronaldo Caiado and marks his first campaign trip to the state for 2026, following Jair Bolsonaro's 2018 and 2022 strategy.

item.title: Lulinha pede a derrubada de vídeos das campanhas de Zema e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), under investigation at the Supreme Federal Court for alleged influence peddling, filed a lawsuit in São Paulo to remove videos by Flávio Bolsonaro and Romeu Zema linking him to INSS fraud schemes. A judge provisionally rejected the request to remove Zema's video, deeming it satirical commentary. The lawsuit against Flávio seeks content removal and R$10,000 in moral damages, claiming defamation through AI-generated material.

item.title: Daniela Lima: Pedido da PGR solucionaria impasse entre Mendonça e PF
item.description: Columnist Daniela Lima suggests that the PGR's request to move the investigation of Fábio Lulinha to first instance could resolve the deadlock between Minister André Mendonça and the Federal Police. She highlighted this possibility on UOL News, indicating that the decision may challenge the differing positions held by the STF and PF.

item.title: Vídeo mostra briga de trânsito no AP; não ataque a ônibus de petistas em SP
item.description: A video circulating on social media misleadingly presents footage of a traffic dispute in Amapá as an attack on a bus carrying PT supporters heading to Lula's campaign launch in São Bernardo do Campo. Fact-checkers confirm the clip has no connection to the political rally or to São Paulo, showing an unrelated road incident with no link to the electoral campaign.
